title: Minimum distance equals minimum nonzero weight
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite field and let $C$ be a linear code of length $n$ over $\alpha$, meaning there is a generator matrix $G$ whose columns generate $C$ (every $G$-image of a message word lies in $C$, and every codeword of $C$ is such an image). Suppose $d$ is the minimum distance of $C$, that is, some two distinct codewords of $C$ lie at Hamming distance exactly $d$ and no two distinct codewords lie closer. Then every nonzero codeword of $C$ has Hamming weight at least $d$, and some codeword of $C$ has Hamming weight exactly $d$, where the weight of a codeword is its Hamming distance from the all-zero codeword.
hypotheses_covered: C is a linear code witnessed by a generator matrix G
d is the minimum Hamming distance of C (attained by some distinct pair, and a lower bound for all distinct pairs)
